name: agent-builder-roster-truthful
body:
`opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` must name exactly the agent roster the suite supports. It must NOT offer or generate an optional `coordinator` primary agent (no roster mention, no `### coordinator (optional)` section, no "whether a coordinator is wanted" interview bullet, no primary-mode scaffold branch, no coordinator example in the register step), and it must NOT generate `implementation-phase-reviewer` (that agent is distributed by `apg init`). Its generated set is the implementers — the core/root `implementer`, per-subsystem `<name>-implementer`s, and tiered `test-implementer`s where a test tier is file-separable — PLUS an OPTIONAL per-repo `release-agent` (see `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-optional-release-agent`), which fills the slot the removed optional `coordinator` vacated. Every generated agent is scaffolded `mode: subagent` with `hidden: true` and `generated: true`.

No generated agent is granted push/tag by default. The ONLY generated agent ever granted `git push`/`git tag` is the optional `release-agent`, and its grant is `ask` (each command prompts for human approval); every other generated agent (the core/root `implementer`, each `<name>-implementer`, and each `test-implementer`) carries NO push/tag grant — the verbs are absent and therefore denied by deny-by-default. That single scoped grant is the deliberate carve-out from the recurring "push/tag remain human-approved acts" law; dispatching the release-agent is gated by the explicit user consent the codebase-navigator captures, so approval surfaces both at dispatch and per command (see `requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out` and `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only`). The word "coordinator" used for the codebase-navigator's ROLE in the feedback-routing/cadence prose is retained — this law forbids only the optional generated AGENT. Satisfaction is assessed by review.
